lines.text: He said no to an order for a hundred thousand radios.
lines.say: He said no to an order for a hundred thousand radios.

lines.text: America, 1955. Akio Morita was selling a tiny radio from a small Japanese company called Sony.
According to Morita, a big American watch company wanted a hundred thousand of them.
A giant order for a tiny company. With one condition.
The radios would carry the buyer's name. Not Sony's.
Back in Tokyo, his board told him to take the deal.
Morita refused. In fifty years, he said, our name will be as famous as yours.
Sony became one of the best-known brands on Earth.
So, would you have taken the money? Or said no?
